Subject: Commercial terms: consumption amortization & overage reconciliation (Globex RFP)

Hi Michael / Procurement team,

Thanks for sending over the RFP sections earlier today. I reviewed Sections 5 and 6 on commercial terms and wanted to propose how Redwood approaches consumption amortization and overage reconciliation so we can slot it into your template without ambiguity. High-level summary: 

- Commit amortization: commits (monthly or annual) are consumed against on-demand usage on a first-in, first-out basis with an ability to smooth seasonal spikes across the term per agreed cadence.
- Overage handling: once committed units are exhausted, overage charges apply at the agreed overage rate. We support monthly true-up or quarterly true-up, depending on your procurement preference.
- Protection mechanics: we can add a small safety buffer (e.g., 5%) that is billed as committed but refundable at renewal or applied to the final true-up to avoid invoice surprises.

Attached is a short worked example spreadsheet showing how amortization and a quarterly true-up would look across a 12-month commit with two typical usage profiles. The attachment also contains sample contract language we recommend for clarity.

Questions for you:
1) Do you prefer monthly or quarterly true-ups for financial reconciliation?
2) Would Globex require prepaid vs. postpaid treatment of committed credits?
3) Any specific procurement constraints around refunds or roll-forward of unused committed units?

If helpful, Ben and Marissa from our finance and sales teams are on copy and can provide the numeric examples and suggested clause text for insertion into your RFP. Happy to jump into a quick call to align.

Best,

Camila Reyes

Thanks Michael — appreciate the constraints, all feasible. Per your points below, here's how Redwood proposes to map contract clauses to your requirements, plus concrete examples. Ben added two bullet items on the proposed pricing numbers for a sample 1M-token/month commit to illustrate economics.

Proposed commercial structure (summary):
- Commit treatment: Annual committed tokens paid upfront at contract signing. We amortize the committed tokens monthly for internal reporting and to enable monthly consumption to draw against the amortized balance. For invoice purposes the commit is prepaid; overages are billed monthly in arrears.
- True-up cadence: Quarterly true-up by default. Any unused committed tokens may be rolled forward one renewal only. Roll-forward is capped at 10% of annual commit; excess unused tokens are forfeited.
- Refunds / credits: Refunds for prepaid committed capacity are allowed only at renewal for cancellations >60 days before renewal and limited to 10% of annual commit value (per your request).
- Safety buffer: We can include a 5% safety cushion of committed tokens as an optional, billable add-on; that buffer is applied before overage pricing.

Sample economics (Ben):
- Example commit: 12M tokens/year (1M/month average). Standard list on-demand rate: $0.0008/token. Committed blended rate proposed: $0.00055/token (approx. 31% discount) with quarterly true-up. Overage rate: $0.0007/token.
- Example outcome: If Q2 usage exceeds amortized commit by 400k tokens, overage for that quarter = 400k * $0.0007 = $280.

Suggested RFP language (drop-in for Section 6):
"Redwood Inference will provide an annual committed token pool payable at contract execution. The committed pool will be amortized on a monthly basis for consumption accounting; invoices will reflect prepaid commit and separate monthly invoices for overages in arrears. Unused committed tokens may be carried forward one renewal cycle up to 10% of the annual committed pool; any amount exceeding 10% is forfeited. Refunds of prepaid committed funds are limited to cancellations submitted >60 days prior to renewal and limited to 10% of the annual committed amount. Quarterly true-ups will reconcile consumption against amortized balances and compute any overage charges at the agreed overage rate."

Next steps:
1) If that language reads OK, Marissa can prepare a short appendix showing the dollar math for the actual commit sizes you indicated in the RFP.
2) We can route a redline through DocuSign for signature once procurement confirms the preferred true-up cadence and payment timing.

Attaching the amortization examples again and the suggested drop-in text as a PDF. Happy to hop on a 30-min call with your finance team if helpful.

Best,

Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

If Globex confirms quarterly true-ups and prepaid annual commit, we're ready to prepare a final commercial appendix and initiate the DocuSign envelope. Link to DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/sign/XYZ-GLX-2027 (placeholder).

Quote from redlined clause for quick copy-paste:
"Customer will prepay the annual committed token pool at contract execution. Redwood will amortize the committed pool monthly for consumption accounting. Quarterly true-ups will reconcile actual usage to amortized balances; overage usage will be invoiced monthly in arrears at the agreed overage rate. Unused committed tokens are eligible for one renewal carry-forward up to 10% of the annual pool; amounts in excess will expire.
